text:
Marina: Hey team — first day setup question. On my M2 mini I installed Homebrew but my PATH looks wrong, `which brew` points to /usr/local/bin/brew but I installed to /opt/homebrew. Also my dotfiles repo expects /usr/local. Any quick fixes?

Theo: Welcome Marina! For Apple Silicon the right path is /opt/homebrew. If your dotfiles hardcode /usr/local you can update the rc or add a symlink: `sudo ln -s /opt/homebrew /usr/local/homebrew` — but I usually prefer adjusting the dotfiles to use $(brew --prefix).

Marina: Thanks. Dotfiles are cloned from git but I'm nervous to change global paths. Is there a recommended minimal patch?

Lena: @Marina easiest is to add this to your ~/.zprofile (or ~/.profile for bash):
```
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
export PATH="$PATH:$(/opt/homebrew/bin)"
```
That keeps it local and matches upstream.

Marina: Nice — done. Next: asdf plugins. The README says `asdf plugin-add nodejs` then `asdf install nodejs latest`, but nodejs plugin needs `gpg` keys imported. On Ventura I get `ERROR: gpg not found`

Sam: Install gpg via brew: `brew install gnupg` then follow the plugin docs: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/install-node -s`. For Apple Silicon you might need `export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` if the install tries to update and hits network rate limits.

Marina: Also trying to get Rust + cargo to match our CI. Should I use rustup or the distro package?

Theo: Use rustup. It matches CI versions and plays nicely with `cargo install` in dev. `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` then add `~/.cargo/bin` to PATH. We pin toolchain with `rust-toolchain.toml` in repo.

Marina: One weird thing: `ssh-agent` isn't forwarding so I can't sign commits with my YubiKey. Any pointers?

Lena: If you're on mac, enable the SSH agent in your keychain and add `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` and `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`. For YubiKey forwarding over WSL/VMs it's messier. If you want, ping infra and we can add you to the docs.

Marina: Cool. Last: envrc vs 1Password. Our repo has an `.envrc` but the onboarding doc suggests storing DB creds in 1Password. What's the workflow?

Sam: We keep secrets in 1Password and use the 1Password CLI in CI. Locally, checkout `.envrc.sample` and source values from 1Password with `op item get 'redwood/dev-db' --fields label=password` then put into `direnv allow`. We avoid committing real env files.

Marina: Perfect. One last ask — where's the dotfiles owner? Want to submit a tiny change to make brew path detection better.

Theo: Ping @infra (infra-bot logged this) or file a tiny PR to `dotfiles/redwood-dotfiles` — owners are listed in the repo. If you post the link here I'll review. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Note: onboarding checklist updated — added Homebrew ARM note and asdf gpg step. https://go.redwood/handbook/onboarding/setup

Marina: Thanks all, fixing the dotfile locally and will open a PR. Appreciate the quick help!
